intro.text: The sergeant in charge of the bridgemen when Kaladin is brought to the Shattered Plains as a slave.
A bridge sergeant in Sadeas's warcamp who has disappeared from the camps without a word.
A former bridge sergeant, now a deserter who has joined Shallan Davar as one of her guards.
A Lightweaver and a member of the Unseen Court, Shallan's band of spies.

items.text: Gaz met Kaladin when he arrived on the Shattered Plains as a slave. When Kaladin said he had been a soldier, Gaz mocked him and nicknamed him "Lordling". Kaladin despised him for neglecting the bridgemen and their gear, and Gaz resented Kaladin for surviving his first bridge run.
Gaz chose new recruits to replace the bridge crews' constant losses, made sure the men did their duties, led them out on bridge runs and kept order.

When Kaladin went to a chasm meaning to end his life, Gaz was oddly sympathetic, though he asked for his vest and sandals. Kaladin came back and threatened him instead, demanding leadership of Bridge Four and his wages, and offering him one mark in five to stay out of his way. After that Gaz paled whenever Kaladin came near.

As Kaladin turned Bridge Four into a real team, the other crews grew resentful. Kaladin persuaded Gaz to switch them to the harder duty of gathering stones; Gaz agreed, then realised he had been tricked and moved them to chasm duty instead.

Gaz's superior, a minor lighteyes named Lamaril, was blackmailing him, and Kaladin's bribes kept Gaz ahead of his payments. Lamaril threatened to make him a bridgeman unless he stopped Kaladin and the new spirit of Bridge Four, so Gaz agreed to bring Kaladin down without making him a martyr.

Seeing Bridge Four practise a side carry, Gaz urged Kaladin to use it, knowing it would end badly. Bridge Four survived, but the move wrecked Sadeas's plan and lost the Alethi the battle. Gaz and Lamaril nearly killed Kaladin on the spot, until he convinced them he was worth more alive, and Lamaril had him beaten instead.

The fallout was severe: over two hundred bridgemen died, Lamaril was executed and Kaladin was strung up in a highstorm. Under his new superior, Hashal, Gaz was treated worse and stripped of his duties. One day he simply stopped turning up, and no one in the camps knew where he had gone.

Gaz and his fellow deserters stayed with Shallan after the fight with the bandits, on her promise of protection and a fresh start. He seemed genuinely happy, became very eager to serve her and even made a window for her wagon, deciding that even uncertain protection beat life as a deserter.
On the Shattered Plains, Gaz and Kaladin met again; Kaladin was still angry, and Gaz ashamed.

Shallan won the deserters a pardon sealed by the king, and Gaz followed her to Sebarial's warcamp, running errands such as searching libraries for books and escorting her. When he saw the portrait she had drawn of him, he wept.
In Urithiru, Shallan paid little attention to her guards, who lost their spark even when Adolin found them work. Her crew dwindled to twelve; Gaz stayed, but spent his days playing cards.

When Shallan saw they needed purpose, she began using them as spies, joining them as Veil without revealing who she was. Gaz's gambling habit remained, kept in check by the rest of the crew. Veil had Ishnah train Gaz, Red and Vathah in spycraft, and the group became the Unseen Court.
Gaz and Shallan's other agents embedded themselves in Ialai Sadeas's warcamp. After Ialai was captured, Gaz and Red searched her bedchamber and found handwritten notebooks and letters.
Gaz was in Urithiru when the singers invaded the tower.

Gaz was one of the Lightweavers helping Shallan infiltrate a Ghostblood meeting at Narak; by now he had bonded a Cryptic. Disguised as crem scrapers, they watched the hideout. When a Ghostblood guard told them to move on, Gaz played an angry foreman so well he drew angerspren, and once the guard was trapped he knocked her out with a chokehold.

appearance.text: A very short Alethi darkeyes of the sixth nahn, with a scarred face where his beard grows only in patches. He lost an eye in unknown circumstances; his other eye is brown. He began wearing an eyepatch only after joining the deserters, and regrew the missing eye with Stormlight once he became a Lightweaver.

personality.text: In Sadeas's camp Gaz hated his role and the suffering it caused, and himself, but had come to see it as the price of survival. With Shallan he wanted to start over and be a better man, found his sense of humour and became loyal to her. In Urithiru, though, he lost his good mood and felt useless.
